heading: Mentor help > Who a mentor is
text: A mentor is a teacher whose class fixed the same mistake that a cohort is working on. Each cohort of fifteen to twenty teachers has one mentor. Some mentors are proven: their class's share of children with the mistake fell clearly from one term to the next and by more than the comparison group's average. Others are candidates: their class has very few children with the mistake while the block average is high, and a method interview comes first.

heading: Mentor help > Who a mentor is
text: A candidate is labelled a candidate until a term confirms it.

heading: Mentor help > How do I record my method
text: Recording a method inside the app is not built yet. The plan is simple: you answer a few questions about how you fixed the mistake, by voice or in writing, and the system turns your own sentences into a method card, keeping your exact words. You read it, change it, and approve it. Until that is built, the mentor page shows where each of your items stands, and your coach can tell you what is waiting.

heading: Mentor help > What happened with my card
text: Each item you submit moves through these states: draft, submitted, awaiting the coach, then changes requested, approved or rejected. An approved item becomes in use only once a published track version includes it. If you edit an item that is in use, a new draft is made and the old one stays in use until the new one is approved. Nothing you record reaches a teacher before the coach approves it.

heading: Mentor help > What does the coach check
text: The coach checks that your card says only what you said, that the steps are safe and plain, that the maths is right, and that nothing identifies a child. A coach can return a card with one reason: wrong maths, culturally off, too complex for the medium, tone issue, or factually shaky. A returned card tells you which.

heading: Mentor help > What you can see
text: You see counts for your own method cards, and a count is shown only if it covers at least five classes. You cannot see which teachers tried your card, and you cannot see any teacher's class.

heading: Mentor help > Your time
text: A mentor's time is capped at about thirty minutes a week.

heading: Mentor help > The cohort thread
text: Your cohort has a small chat thread. Names are pseudonyms, no phone numbers or handles are shown, and a child's name cannot be posted. You can answer a teacher's question there. The coach moderates the thread. The assistant never writes a post in the thread.

heading: Mentor help > Papers: create, import and assign
text: You can create a paper from the rules or import one from a PDF or an answered sheet, as a teacher does, and assign a paper to teachers inside the cohorts you mentor. Only the printed questions of an upload are read: handwriting and names are ignored and not kept, and the upload is deleted when you confirm or after 24 hours. Code computes every answer key; a person confirms every item.

heading: Mentor help > Papers: create, import and assign
text: A pre-test goes to teachers or classes, because cohorts form from its results; a post-test or termly check can go to a cohort, which creates one assignment for each class in it. A post-test is assigned with the pre-test it twins, and you are warned if that pre-test was not assigned.

heading: Mentor help > Papers: create, import and assign
text: A paper must be approved or confirmed to be assigned, an active assignment is one for each class, paper and kind, and an assignment cannot be withdrawn once a sheet is entered. You see progress as counts only: assigned, opened, sheets entered and completed. The assistant asks about anything missing, such as who, when and which kind, and prepares a draft you review; only you press Assign. The basics are the same as for a teacher.

heading: Mentor help > Papers: create, import and assign
text: A paper is the printed set of questions; a check is one use of it in your class. They are separate jobs, so you make or bring in a paper on the Papers page, and Enter check only asks you to choose one. Open Papers and tap Create a paper. There are two ways.

heading: Mentor help > Papers: create, import and assign
text: Generate from rules: code builds the paper from the approved rules, from your last check's class counts, from four short questions about your class, or the standard paper. The first ten items are anchors, the same skills and level on every paper, and before and after are compared only on these; up to five adaptive items go deeper on what your class finds hard and never count as improvement.

heading: Mentor help > Papers: create, import and assign
text: From a PDF or an answered sheet: upload a PDF or up to three photos of a paper you already used. Only the printed questions are read. Handwriting and names are ignored and not kept, and the upload is deleted when you confirm, or after 24 hours. The AI reads the questions; it never gives an answer key.

heading: Mentor help > Papers: create, import and assign
text: Code works out every correct answer, the error each item can show and the grid of which items check which error, and a printed key that differs is flagged, never trusted. You confirm every item before the paper can be used. An item the system cannot score yet, such as a word problem, is listed as not supported: leave it out or enter it by hand. A dictated item needs the number that was said.

heading: Mentor help > Papers: create, import and assign
text: An imported paper says Imported, awaiting review until a reviewer confirms it, and it is not printed by the system because it is already printed. Enter check uses the chosen paper's own key, worked out by code from its numbers, so an imported paper is entered like any other. Once the first sheet is entered the paper is frozen and cannot change: make a new version instead. Each paper shows whether cohorts have formed.

heading: Mentor help > Papers: create, import and assign
text: If not, it says why and what to do next: no check has used the paper yet, a check is open with some sheets entered, every sheet is entered and not yet approved, approved but not closed, or submitted and waiting for other classes with the same error. A pre-test cannot go to a cohort, because cohorts form from its results. Papers assigned to you show at the top of Papers and in Enter check.

heading: Mentor help > Papers: create, import and assign
text: The assistant asks one question at a time about anything missing, such as the class, the kind, the form or an unclear number, and fills in the draft from your answers. It marks what it changed with an Undo, and it never confirms, approves or assigns: you press those.

heading: Mentor help > How is the next module chosen?
text: Code chooses it; the AI only words it. After module 1 the teacher plays it or marks it heard, then answers Tried it, Partly or Not yet, with an optional note (a child's name is removed before it is saved). Then she can press Generate next module, and the coach can press it for her. Tried it gives the next module in the track. Partly gives the same approach again, as a smaller step with more practice.

heading: Mentor help > How is the next module chosen?
text: Not yet gives another approach for the same mistake from the strategy library, leaving out the approaches she has already had. If she has not answered by the set date (3 days in the demo), the planned next module is queued, and her silence is never counted as a result. Call 5 words the module from the approved module topic and strategies; if no draft comes back, code writes it from the same content.

heading: Mentor help > How is the next module chosen?
text: Every module goes to the coach's review queue before it reaches her, voiced in her language with her class's numbers filled in by code. A failed voice leaves the text, with a retry.

heading: Mentor help > The cohort chat
text: Open Cohort chat and choose your cohort. You see the cohort's thread and an Open questions tab with the questions still waiting. A reply from you cancels the AI's answer for that question; a reply from a teacher does not. You can share tips, reply and mark a question resolved. Only the coach can correct an AI answer, hide or pin a message, or change how long the AI waits.
